Basically, they are switching you form "employee" to "independent contractor." For tax purposes, you will have to account for your own FICA and Medicare (both sides, not just 50% like now), as well as federal state and local income taxes. You will also need to buy and maintain your own health insurance, life insurance, etc. DO THE NUMBERS. I cannot stress this enough. You have to know what the extra cost is, and how much you need to charge to cover this.

You also need to know how much they are saving. Often you will get a "true cost/full disclosure" of your pay. Not sure if this is a requirement, but the last 2 companies I have worked for have provided this. The company gets you off their tax rolls, off their insurance costs, etc. They just have to cut you a check as any other vendor, meaning that your "paycheck" is just another "invoice" to them - they are not by law required to pay you special over any other vendor, and in fact, less so, since you are small potatoes. You will lose the paycheck protection that being on the payroll has. You will need to account for your time more accurately now, as you have to justify your invoices, in case they dispute it. You will have to follow up with AP if they don't cut your check right away. You will need to send in invoices in a timely and organized manner. You will need to maintain your own acocunting system to calculate payroll taxes, income taxes, keep track of your health care, make payments, etc. - you are now a small business. Get Quickbooks if nothing else and LEARN TO USE IT PROPERLY.

I have friends who went consultancy and loved it, as their income skyrocketed, and they felt closer to the business, as their livelihood now depended on being really good at tracking things. Additionally, there is no restriction to selling yourself to others now. You now get paid directly to the amount of work and value you provide. He was able to provide 40 hours at "old job" AND sell himself 20-25 hours to another company, working mornings, nights and weekends. At rates he never dreamed possible.
